subject: Linguistics
title: The Mental Lexicon
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Mental Lexicon usable.

hook.text: You know about 50,000 words—and can retrieve any one in less than 200 milliseconds.

buildup.text: The mental lexicon is your brain's dictionary—organized not alphabetically but by meaning and sound.

discovery.text: Words are linked by meaning (dog→cat), sound (dog→log), and association (dog→bone).

twist.text: The tip-of-the-tongue state proves the lexicon is real—you know the word exists but can't find it.

climax.text: Priming studies show that hearing 'doctor' speeds up recognition of 'nurse.'

punchline.text: Your brain's dictionary has no alphabet—just connections.

quiz.question: How is the mental lexicon organized?
options: By meaning and sound networks, not alphabetically
